Judgment calls: (a) This drafter marks a wire CROSSOVER by putting a square/U-shaped dip in the horizontal wire where it meets a vertical, and draws real junctions as filled or small open circles. There are exactly two such dips: at (107,290) where the ground->R13 wire meets the n5 spur, and at (322,375) where the Diode15-Diode14 wire meets the R11 column. Both are read as crossovers (no connection). Reading the (107,290) dip as a junction would tie the collector of BJT 2 to its own emitter (both would be net 0) and kill the device, which is the classic sign of a mis-read crossing; reading the (322,375) dip as a junction would tie the diode string to the +5V/+6V divider. Both dips are drawn identically, so one convention covers both. (b) Consequence of (a): net n5 ends in a bare wire end at (107,312). That is a real dead-end drawn by the drafter, not a mis-trace; n5 still has two component terminals (BJT2 collector, BJT5 collector), so nothing is left dangling electrically and no component is marked unconnected. (c) Transistor symbols are all drawn with a straight base bar, the base lead entering perpendicular on one side of the bar and collector+emitter leaving from the two ends on the other side; the emitter is the lead carrying the little arrowhead. That fixes: BJT 0 base = up to n1, emitter = the right/lower lead to n2, collector = the left lead to 0; BJT 7 base = up to n2, emitter = right lead to n7, collector = left lead to n3; BJT 5 base = down to n6, emitter = up-right lead to n10, collector = up-left lead to n5; BJT 6 base = up to n12, emitter = down-right lead to n11, collector = down-left lead to n15; BJT 1 base = the curve (n4), emitter = up-left lead to 0, collector = up-right lead to n3; BJT 3 base = up to n15, emitter = down-left lead to 0, collector = down-right lead to n11; BJT 4 base = up to n14, emitter = down-left lead to n11, collector = down-right lead to n9. (d) BJT-NPN 2 is the one genuinely awkward symbol: its base bar is the short horizontal at y~210 spanning x 93-117, the base lead is the free-hand curve leaving upward at x~95 (net n4), and the two lower leads are the diagonal down-left to the left rail and the diagonal down-right (branching at x~107) to the (136,224) dot. There is an arrow-like blob at the far end of the down-left lead (x 81-88, y 217-219), matching where BJT 1's emitter arrow sits, so the down-left lead to the left rail is read as the emitter and the down-right lead as the collector. This is the reading that also makes BJT 1 and BJT 2 a sensible pair (both emitters on the ground rail, bases tied). (e) Diode terminal order is index 0 = cathode (the bar, drawn on the left for both diodes; both triangles point left) and index 1 = anode. (f) All five V-DC (one port) symbols are the labelled arrows (+3V id16, +15V id17, +5V id18, +10V id20, +6V id21); each has a single lead onto the net named above. (g) Every open circle in this drawing sits where three or more wires meet ((53,276), (373,149), (243,419), (324,421)) and is read as a junction, same as a filled dot.
